title: Red Dead Redemption 2
provenance: tested locally on Apple Silicon (M1 Pro), macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r5, 2026-09-10: loads to 98 per cent and never renders. Status stays community because there is no verdict for a title we tested and could not run.
notes: Does not run on this Mac as of 2026-09-10 (M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r5), and both of its renderers now have a precise, reproducible failure. VULKAN (the game's default): the Rockstar launcher signs in, RDR2 opens a 1280x720 window, loads to 98 per cent, creates its swapchain and exits without a frame, because MoltenVK 1.4.1 refuses 'vkCreateImage(): If tiling is VK_IMAGE_TILING_LINEAR, mipLevels must be 1' (3) and 'imageType must be VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D' (16), with MoltenVK's shader translator also emitting uncompilable Metal (gl_CullDistance in an undeclared struct member) and about 10900 AGX bytes_per_row assertions along the way. Identical on every run. DIRECTX 12 can be selected and reached, which took the whole evening to establish: there is no -dx12 switch (the exe knows -vulkan, -ignoreDifferentVideoCard, -safemode, -ignorepipelinecache); the API is set only in Documents/Rockstar Games/Red Dead Redemption 2/Settings/system.xml, as <API>kSettingAPI_DX12</API> inside the <advancedGraphics> block, in a complete file (root rage__fwuiSystemSettingsCollection, version 37, configSource kSettingsConfig_Safe, taken from files the game wrote on Windows). With that file the game does load d3d12.dll, but the Rockstar launcher needs DXMT's Direct3D 11 (it loads d3d11/d3d10core/dxgi only from system32, never from its own folder) while the game needs a D3D12 provider, and one process tree has one search path. The configuration that gives both what they need: graphics mode DXMT, and on the Steam program a WINEDLLPATH_PREPEND listing the dxmt and d9vk directories first and the d3dmetal directory after them, so d3d11 resolves to DXMT for the launcher and d3d12, which DXMT does not ship, falls through to D3DMetal for the game, plus CX_D3DMETALPATH and the DYLD fallback paths pointing at D3DMetal's external folder. Under that, the launcher signs in, RDR2 initialises D3DMetal (the framework, its IR converter and winemetal all load into RDR2.exe) and for the first time creates no Vulkan swapchain and logs no MoltenVK error at all. It then dies about 30 seconds in: D3DMetal answers a Direct3D 12 call with 'err: Not implemented', and the game faults on an execute access to 0x20019008070c10, a garbage function pointer, the same address with and without Highball's timestamp shim, so the shim is not the cause and the missing call is inside Apple's Game Porting Toolkit. Winedbg gives no backtrace. Which D3D12 method is unimplemented is the one open question, and a stub for it in the timestamp shim (which already patches D3DMetal vtable slots) is the plausible fix, if it can be identified. Vulkan cannot be removed to force anything: RDR2.exe hard-imports ffx_fsr2_api_vk_x64.dll, which hard-imports vulkan-1.dll. Disabling amd_ags_x64 kills the process outright (RDR2.exe imports it statically), unlike Guardians of the Galaxy.

knownIssues.symptom: On its default Vulkan renderer: loads to about 98 per cent, opens a window, exits without a frame. On DirectX 12 (selectable only through system.xml): D3DMetal initialises, then the game crashes about 30 seconds in.
knownIssues.cause: Vulkan: MoltenVK 1.4.1 refuses the game's linear-tiled mipmapped images. DirectX 12: Apple's D3DMetal answers a D3D12 call the game needs with 'Not implemented' and the game calls through the result (execute fault at 0x20019008070c10).
knownIssues.fix: none today. Both are engine work: a MoltenVK change, or identifying and stubbing the unimplemented D3D12 call in the timestamp shim that already fronts D3DMetal.
